ops.title: Phase 0 — embedding engine as a shared module, wasm fetched at runtime
ops.description:
Extract cc-context's `semsearch` types + `cache` + `embed` + `rank` (~1,700 LOC, external surface ≈ wazero + `golang.org/x/sys`) into the nested module `github.com/yasyf/cc-context/semsearch` (note `acd2aac` §4). The `internal/backend` god-struct tangle stays confined to `engine`, which cc-notes skips.

Use `WebPin` (`potion-base-8M`), not `CodePin` — notes are prose. Zero tree-sitter and zero zig: markdown already takes the line-chunking path, and `internal/web/chunk.go` is a better prose chunker and pure Go (goldmark, heading-aware with breadcrumbs, 768-token packing, never splits inside fenced code). Port that, skip `chunk/`.

The wasm rides the hardened pinned-weights path (note `acd2aac` §1). Pre-seed weights and wasm at install so the first session is not the one that pays. Namespace or version-pin the wazero AOT cache dir — it is keyed by a wazero version string that resolves to the literal `"dev"` for non-release builds, so two binaries can collide in one directory.

Shell-out to `ccx` is REJECTED, not deferred: no arbitrary-string embed API, a process spawn plus module compile per call, one query per process so the resident cache always misses. If extraction stalls, vendor the four packages into `internal/` — faster, at the cost of forking the golden-parity suite and the pins, which are load-bearing correctness.

ops.text: CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./... green in both repos from a fresh clone with no Rust toolchain
go list succeeds on the module-proxy copy of cc-context (it fails today)
The nested module's go list -m all shows no unexpected dependency
Vectors are byte-identical to cc-context's on a shared fixture, and the golden-parity suite still passes
